content.text:
`sort_a` is faster on 100k random ints, about 2.4× quicker than `sort_b`. I wrote `faster: sort_a` to `RESULT.md`.

I ran both on the same 100k random ints (seed 0, values 0–10⁹), three runs each, taking the fastest run. I also checked that both outputs match `sorted()`.

| function | method | best time |
|---|---|---|
| `sort_a` | top-down merge sort, O(n log n) | 0.181 s |
| `sort_b` | `bisect.insort` into a growing list | 0.428 s |

`sort_b` loses because each insert has to shift the rest of the list, so it does O(n²) total work. That shifting runs in C, which keeps it from losing by more at this size; the gap should grow as n gets larger. That last point is an inference — I only measured n = 100k.
